title: ‘Ted Lasso’ Star Jason Sudeikis Goes One-on-One With WNBA Great Breanna Stewart (Watch)
full_text: Skip to main content Breaking News Done Deal: Paramount Completes Warner Bros. Takeover, Creating Hollywood Giant close Jason Sudeikis is a fixture of CeLIBrity row, the group of famous New York Liberty fans who go to see Breanna Stewart dominate the opposition. They were photographed Sept. 16 at Splashlight Studios in New York. Sudeikis: Styling by Keith Wagner; God’s True Cashmere shirt; Todd Snyder pants; Nike sneakers; Sudeikis’ T-shirt, cap, watch. Stewart: Styling by Jan-Michael Quammie; Stone Island top, jeans; Stewart’s shoes, jewelry. Photographed by Nina Westervelt; Sudeikis grooming: Chelsea Gehr. Stewart hair: Antoinette Hill; Makeup: Sofia Nikolic “Stewie!” When the New York Liberty’s star forward Breanna Stewart shows up on the THR set, all 6-feet-4 of her, Jason Sudeikis reaches up to embrace her. It’s the kind of hug he’s given her courtside after the team’s major victories, including during their run to the 2024 WNBA championship. The four-time Emmy winner, who played college basketball in his native Kansas before going into comedy and becoming Saturday Night Live’ s resident jock, doesn’t do fandom halfway. It’s why, today, he refuses to remove his Arsenal hat; he became a hard-core supporter of the Premier League team while in London shooting Ted Lasso , which in its fourth season sees the irrepressibly upbeat coach leading a women’s soccer team. It’s why he’s wearing Nikes in UConn colorways to honor Stewart’s alma mater. And it’s why he’s become a fixture of CeLIBrity row, the group of Liberty superfans that includes Spike Lee, Alicia Keys and the cast of Severance . Related Stories TV 'Ted Lasso' Takes the Express Lane in Season 4's Penultimate Episode TV WNBA Playoffs 2026: Where to Watch Post-Season Women's Basketball Games Live Online There are few accomplishments in basketball that Stewart has not achieved. She has four NCAA titles, one WNBA title, four World Cup championships and three Olympic gold medals. The 32-year-old is far from done. “I want to beat all the records,” she tells Sudeikis. Who are we to doubt her? A week after her sit-down with Sudeikis, the eight-seed Liberty will sweep top-seed Minnesota Lynx in the playoffs, toppling the team led by Stewart’s friend and former UConn teammate Napheesa Collier, with whom she co-founded the successful 3-on-3 offseason league Unrivaled in 2023. In this third edition of THR ‘s Game Recognize Game series, Stewart and Sudeikis discuss the surprising parallels in their career paths, the ways in which the WNBA is handling the scrutiny since superstar Caitlin Clark’s arrival ushered in millions of new fans but also culture-war insanity in a league that’s long been a haven of inclusivity, and how she would realistically handle having Ted Lasso as a coach. JASON SUDEIKIS Nice to see you in street clothes. BREANNA STEWART I know, right? We never do this. SUDEIKIS And you never see me out of Liberty gear. We’re doing THR ‘s Game Recognize Game . Athlete, artist, artistic athlete, athletic artist, I’d like to think. … How are the gigs similar? I have my theories, but I’m more interested in what you think. STEWART Well, people ask me why I want to continue to be great, or how I keep winning. There’s this obsessiveness of continuing to go and try to be better. Like, almost an insane confidence. SUDEIKIS Yeah. It doesn’t feel like ambition from the inside. It just feels like, if I have the opportunity to get to continue to do this, why not do it as best as I can, until I can no longer do it? With athletics, though, it seems like, oh, eventually someone younger comes in, with better knees, more athletic, whatever. Rarely is it that they’re hungrier. I don’t know of anybody that’s been in your position that’s just like, “Oh, fuck it, I give up. Let them have it.” That doesn’t happen. STEWART No. Especially when a new person comes in, you’re like, “Oh, I’m going to sauce them.” Like, “Oh, they’re in for a long night.” SUDEIKIS How has the college system changed? It feels like, even from my small understanding, [UConn coach Geno] Auriemma softened in his relationship to the players — we all saw Paige [Bueckers], you know, smack him on the butt. Jason Sudeikis Photographed by Nina Westervelt STEWART He’s so, so soft. Coach Auriemma is so soft. SUDEIKIS Lorne, Lorne Michaels at SNL , I feel like has softened up, too. STEWART When I went to college­ — when I went to UConn, Coach Auriemma was tough. He was an ass. He was really an ass. I was a 17-, 18-year-old that thought I was working hard — and then he just kind of chopped me down. SUDEIKIS Did it help when you look back on it now? Do you go, “Oh, it was worth it”? STEWART It helped. I wouldn’t be where I am without Coach Auriemma. Of course. Did it always need to be like that? Mm, no. SUDEIKIS Same with Lorne, yeah. Has that changed? STEWART Yes. I think the NIL [name-image-likeness] landscape makes it different. He had to soften to keep people around. You could just transfer and not have to sit out. You get paid hundreds of thousands of dollars — millions — to be places. So [as a coach], you’ve got to be nice. SUDEIKIS Exactly! Any idea how that’s going to affect those same 17-, 18-year-olds that you were? Beyond the winning, you get to feel like hot shit. You can go, “Look, Coach, you have to listen to me ’cause I have 250,000 followers. These are my apostles. I am God. They will come after you. They will dox you.” STEWART I think what’s happening with the generation going to college now, their why is not the same. Because my why was, well, I want to be the best player that ever leaves UConn, and I’m going to win four national championships … Breanna Stewart Photographed by Nina Westervelt SUDEIKIS Which you did. No big deal. STEWART … and I want to be great. But, like, their why now is, “Well, I want to get deals. I want to get this money.” That’s my assumption. But when you have the money just being flaunted in front of your face, you’re thinking about it. SUDEIKIS We both come from what are, from the outside view, these cults: SNL and UConn. It teaches you to work hard, probably harder than you thought you needed to. It is the hardest job I ever had. I was there 10 years. I would not be where I am without it. STEWART SNL is incredible. How did that start? SUDEIKIS I mean, it’s not too dissimilar from the journey of a blue-chip athlete on the way in. There are different places that they come and scout. There’s The Groundlings in Los Angeles, that’s where Will Ferrell started or Kristen Wiig. UCB here in New York, where Amy Poehler came from, and a bunch of people behind the scenes. I did a thing called Second City in Chicago. Tina Fey did that. Chris Farley, John Belushi, Gilda Radner back in the day. I was on, like, their JV team, the touring company. A fella named Jeff Richmond, who is Tina Fey’s husband, came out to see our show in Las Vegas. And he was like, “Hey, you ever thought about auditioning for SNL ?” And, at that point, I was like, “No way, Jose. I don’t like that show. I ain’t that.” It was mostly me being a 22-year-old dickhead that was like, “I don’t want something that would never want me.” But I auditioned for it in, like, 2003, and got hired as a writer. Later I had a meeting with Lorne my second year — my sophomore year. I mentioned to him, like, “Hey, you know, to do this, I gave up performing. I’d still really like to do that.” STEWART Yeah. Put me in the game. SUDEIKIS The next show, Tom Brady hosted, and I got to do a bit in one of the scenes that I wrote where I did like the Running Man and the Roger Rabbit and all those silly dances that I still do — that I’ve done on Ted Lasso , that I used to do to make kids on my basketball team laugh. And he put me in the cast, like, two weeks after that. What is it like when Coach says, “Hey, come play for us”? Jason Sudeikis and Breanna Stewart Photographed by Nina Westervelt (2) STEWART It’s not like he’s offering formally. He’s like, “I think you should be here. This place is going to be what makes you better.” And then he’s like, “Well, are you going to come?” SUDEIKIS Did any other place have a shot at you? STEWART Like, for real? I looked at Duke. Beautiful campus. I looked at Maryland, I looked at Penn State. Those were my tops. But no, I wanted to be great. I looked at all the players that came before me and where they were now, and UConn was the only place. SUDEIKIS Fort Scott Community College was the height of my basketball and scholastic career. Which kind of segues into how you kindly invited me to go work out with you with [trainer] Chris Brickley two years ago. STEWART That was great. We should go do that again. SUDEIKIS I’ve never had any kind of masculine macho arrogance of, like, men’s sports versus women’s sports. But if any of that did ever course through my brain and body and soul, it would’ve been eliminated after that afternoon. You’re so good. Like, and you’re so effortlessly good. You’ve been so good for so long that you’re just iconic. … You’re like the Jennifer Aniston of the WNBA. You know what I mean? STEWART Period! Yes. I want to be her. You’ve got to bring her to a game. OK? Thanks. SUDEIKIS I would love to. I think she’s in London right now. STEWART I’m going to write that in my notes: “Bring Jen Aniston to game . “ Handle that. Jason Sudeikis and Breanna Stewart Photographed by Nina Westervelt SUDEIKIS But as we were leaving [the workout], we were just chatting about where [the WNBA] was going, and all these eyeballs, which at least in the past four or five years, sort of gets pushed through the prism of Caitlin [Clark]. And you had said this really wise thing: “We’ve all wanted this success, but with success comes trouble.” And it makes me think of this Nietzsche quote [as paraphrased in Ted Lasso ], “Once you’re at the top of the mountain, what’s left for you but lightning?” You, I think, personally have avoided a lot of that lightning. Why do you think some folks get it and some folks don’t? STEWART I think that the discourse just comes because of the climate. It’s like, if you want the fame and the popularity and the notoriety and all that stuff, like you have to take the good with the bad. SUDEIKIS What’s your relationship with social media? Because that is one of the turbo boosters with all of this. STEWART I’m not doing that. I’m not looking for that. Are you? Do you look for that stuff? SUDEIKIS No. I did for a little bit. STEWART I control what I can control. I detach from judgment. SUDEIKIS That’s a harder thing. It’s very intoxicating, new fame. That was one of those things that I got to view at SNL . If you go seek validation from it, then when they come for you on the other side of it, I think it could just destroy your soul, potentially. STEWART Someone said to me, “Unless I’m going to go to these same people who are telling me how I’m bad at basketball and ask them how I should be parenting my kids, it doesn’t matter.” SUDEIKIS We had our own version of backlash in our little neck of the woods with Ted Lasso . But the discourse doesn’t change the way we go about making the show, for better or worse. And I don’t know how much any of this stuff, these outside influences, affect a locker room. STEWART Well, what I’m having to tell my teammates more and more is to make sure you’re prepared. Don’t let these questions catch you off guard. Obviously, there’s a lot of media surrounding the WNBA, and people are trying to kind of ride the wave, the trajectory of where we’re going. So, now, you’re not only thinking about the next game or next matchup or how am I going to get to the playoffs, but also you have to be ready for the questions that are going to come that are completely outside the court. SUDEIKIS One thing I’ve noticed [going to WNBA games] is that negativity [in the stands], up until maybe this past season, gets rejected like a foreign body in the human. Sudeikis embracing Stewart at a Liberty game in July Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images STEWART I remember when you guys first came to the game. It was 2023. Things are going good, the energy at Barclays is incredible. It’s my first year there. And my teammates were like, “Ted Lasso’s here! We need to get a picture!” Then you brought your kids. You came back. And now, we’re your team. SUDEIKIS A hundred percent, yeah. I remember you early on busting my balls about, like, “Who are you going to cheer for when we play against the [Indiana] Fever [Caitlin Clark’s team]? STEWART Sorry, you can’t come in and cheer for the Fever. We’ll have you removed. SUDEIKIS So you just won, what, your fourth gold medal? STEWART My fourth World Cup medal. SUDEIKIS I went on Wikipedia knowing we were going to do this, and holy moly, it takes three swipes to get through all your [achievements] from your high school days to three days ago. Like, when’s enough enough? ( Laughs. ) STEWART It’s never enough. First of all, I want to beat [four-time WNBA champion, former UConn Husky and Stewart’s former Seattle Storm teammate] Sue [Bird]. So right now I’ve just tied Sue. [ Editor’s note: Stewart beat Bird’s record the following week to become the league’s eighth all-time leading scorer. ] I think winning is addicting. When you win awards and whatnot, you want to do it again, right? When we won here in New York, the parade was insane, and I want to do it again. SUDEIKIS It’d be badass if we pulled it off this year. STEWART Never say never. I plan on playing for a while. I’m newly 32. Virgo. SUDEIKIS The Magic Johnson year. STEWART Yeah, my Magic Johnson year. I want to just keep winning. Stewart at Barclays Center in September Elsa/Getty Images SUDEIKIS I want to ask you about your league, Unrivaled. What was the impetus? It reminds me of the heyday of United Artists and Charlie Chaplin. As I understand it, people were upset with the studio system, specifically actors and the artists themselves, and so they created United Artists. From the outside looking in, there’s a [similar] element to Unrivaled in giving power back to the player. STEWART We’ve exceeded expectations. We have a valuation of $650 million. That’s higher than some WNBA valuations. With Unrivaled, we had the special opportunity to start something new, bring a platform back to the United States, back to our home market during the WNBA offseason, and also pay the players. Give them equity. A league made by players for players. And selling it [to investors] was hard. Like, when you have to sell your show, it’s hard, right? Nobody believes in it. SUDEIKIS Oh my gosh, yeah. We went out to everyone, but only one place [bid for it], Apple. STEWART Yeah. In the beginning, that was the hardest, because you have to get outside investors to believe something that’s just a blueprint. And they’re like, “Well, why is this going to work?” But it starts with the players that agreed to be in it in year one. The strength in numbers is the biggest thing in women’s basketball. SUDEIKIS There was some quote from Del Close, who was an improv guru and a teacher I had for a year before he passed away: “The worst idea with full support will always beat the best idea with no support.” It’s the exact same thing as showbiz. You have this idea about, you know, this universe where people fight with lightsabers and it’s like, I don’t know. “Just do it and give me money on the back end with the action figures.” Like, “OK, dummy.” And then, ha ha, now he has a museum. STEWART So, some people have said that Ted Lasso was dead [after season three]. SUDEIKIS Like, literally? STEWART The show. Not the coach. Hopefully he does not have a heart attack or anything in the finale. SUDEIKIS You’re going to have to watch. Sudeikis (left) as Ted Lasso, and Brendan Hunt as his right-hand man, Coach Beard, in Ted Lasso season four. Courtesy of Apple TV+ STEWART But what made you want to focus on women’s soccer this season? Is it because of the rise in women’s sports? SUDEIKIS It certainly helped open my eyes to it. It’s that experience of those seats we’ve had [at Liberty games at the Barclays Center] the last three seasons and watching these women walk on and off the court that just feels so … gooey with story complexity. When I thought [the show] was done, it really was done. But I just kept hearing the characters’ voices. So it was important for me to just keep jotting down these ideas, and at some point it became too silly — it would almost be selfish — to not do it. STEWART So is there going to be a season five? SUDEIKIS I don’t know. That was smooth. That was smooth. STEWART That scene [in season four] when you went in the women’s locker room with the trash can on your head? That was funny. I really enjoyed that. If Ted Lasso was my coach for the Liberty, I think it would be funny. SUDEIKIS I think we’d have a good time. I don’t know, would you be annoyed? STEWART Maybe. title: Amazon Strikes Six-Year Global Deal For Emmys Worth More Than $20M Per Year, Will Make Event Free To View
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News $110B Merger Of Paramount & Warner Bros Discovery Officially Closes Read the full story By Peter White Peter White Executive Editor, Television @peterzwhite More Stories By Peter Conan O’Brien, Bowen Yang & Shane Gillis Podcasts Become Golden Globe Eligible As Shortlist Revealed Amazon Hires Three Netflix Business Affairs Execs As It Moves To Genre-Based Model Alcon Eyes UK Series Adaptations Of ‘Insomnia’, ‘Prisoners’ & ‘P.S. I Love You’ After Launch Of Diego Piasek-Run International Studio Arm View All October 6, 2026 6:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Emmys Frazer Harrison/Getty Images The Emmys officially have a new rights holder. Amazon on Tuesday closed its deal with the Television Academy , as previewed last month , and it’s a significant pact. The partnership gives Prime Video the right to stream the annual TV awards ceremony for the next six years and is thought to be worth north of $120 million in total. The streamer has taken global rights to the event but will make it free to view on its Prime Video service each September. Related Stories News Amazon In Talks To Take Over Emmys TV Deal Below The Line 2026-27 Awards Season Calendar: Oscars, Emmys, Grammys, Guilds & More Deadline understands that the deal is worth between $20M-$25M per year, with one source pegging the value at $24M per year. Watch on Deadline The deal succeeds the broadcast wheel, which has seen broadcast networks ABC, CBS, Fox and NBC rotate the rights to air the ceremony each year. That system has been in place for over 30 years, since 1995. Mike Hopkins, head of Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios, told Deadline that it wanted to create a “global event” on Prime Video. “We thought we could increase the viewership, bring in a younger audience, work with the Academy to put a lot more energy, and maybe look at the production itself to try to innovate,” he said. “I feel that we can put the Emmys on a path to global growth and relevance that was probably harder to do when it was spinning from network to network and then distributed in various ways around the world.” The global nature of the deal is interesting, particularly given the fee increase the TV Academy has secured. The broadcast networks have paid between $8M-$10M per year to air in the U.S., but it’s not clear how much revenue the Academy makes from international broadcasters. The event has aired live in a number of international markets including on CTV in Canada, Showcase in Australia, Canal+ in France, TNT across Latin America and Sky Italia, but in many territories it is aired and streamed on smaller services and networks. Television Academy chair Cris Abrego added that he didn’t want to just renew the wheel deal. “I felt strongly from the outset that this was an opportunity to rethink the model,” he said. “Starting every year with a new partner, trying to find a production partner, a brand partner, trying to bring even the simpleness of learnings from the past event into the next year didn’t matter because of the different institutions… that was very challenging. As television and the industry is evolving, the telecast and much like the Academy needed to evolve, and so having a singular home was my goal from the outset.” Former Banijay Americas boss Abrego said that making the show free to view, and not behind a paywall, was a “non-negotiable” for the Academy. “I give Mike credit. From our early conversations, he understood that. It’s not simply just about distributing an award show, they really understood what the Emmys mean to the television community and what we could build around that and we’re really excited about it,” he added. Amazon has put other events in front of the paywall including a number of Amazon Fire concerts and its Black Friday NFL game. Hopkins pointed to the fact that the company has a “very large ad business.” “We have we have a variety of other economic levers we can pull to make it make financial sense for us. We also have nearly all of the streaming services as part of Prime Video in our subscription business, and many of this year’s winners are available to our Prime Video customers via driving to HBO Max or Apple TV. We see it as something that sits as part of our entertainment system with customers where we can celebrate these awards and nominees throughout the year. We can be the home of many of the best shows on television today, not just those that we make ourselves, but our partners are the ones that are always every year going to get the lion’s share of awards,” he said. Amazon itself hasn’t performed particularly well at the Emmys over the last few years; this year, largely thanks to Spider-Noir, which also aired on MGM+, it scored 10 wins; last year, it won five awards at the Creative Arts Emmys and in 2024 it won four.

title: Skydancing At Last: $110B Merger Of Paramount And Warner Bros Discovery Officially Closes
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News $110B Merger Of Paramount & Warner Bros Discovery Officially Closes Read the full story By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Skydancing At Last: $110B Merger Of Paramount And Warner Bros Discovery Officially Closes ESPN & HBO Vet Bomani Jones Teams With Playmaker For Long-Running Podcast ‘The Right Time’ WBD’s JB Perrette Makes The Leap To Skydance: Here Is Why Zaslav’s Lieutenant Ended Up In Ellison’s Executive Suite View All October 6, 2026 5:59am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Story Arc The long-gestating merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery officially closed Tuesday, yielding a new major player in media. Shares in the combined company, Skydance , will start trading later in the day on the New York Stock Exchange. Shares of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery have been discontinued on the Nasdaq. Related Stories News New Skydance Sets Top Executive Structure As Paramount-WBD Merger Set To Close Executives Ynon Kreiz Anointed Co-CEO Of New Paramount-WBD; David Ellison Says Mega-Studio Is “Transformational Moment For Our Industry” The closing brings to an end a year-long saga over who would control two century-old movie studios along with a pedigreed stable of TV studios, streaming services and networks including HBO and CNN. Now, attention will turn to the difficult economics faced by the new company. It starts off with some $80 billion in debt and an ambitious plan to convert a traditional media company into a tech-oriented operation capable of measuring up to Netflix, Amazon and Disney. Larry Ellison, the billionaire co-founder of Oracle, is a key backer of Skydance. His son, David Ellison , an actor-turned-producer who has made a dramatic entrance to the Hollywood corporate scene at just 43 years old, is running the company as chairman and CEO. Watch on Deadline “Today is a historic day, not just for Skydance but for our entire industry,” David Ellison said in a statement. “From the start, our ambition was to bring these two storied studios together and create a stronger competitor, with the talent, resources, and reach to tell great stories in every genre, on every platform, for audiences everywhere. Now that ambition is a reality. We’re grateful to everyone who made this possible – the employees, creative talent, and production teams of both companies, who worked tirelessly to get us here and inspire audiences around the world every day, as well as the advisors and partners who guided this transaction to completion. Our focus now turns to the future: building a company that empowers creatives, entertains audiences and rewards shareholders. We couldn’t be more excited to get to work.” Gerry Cardinale, a Skydance board member and key financier via his firm, RedBird Capital, called the merger close “a defining moment for the industry. By applying our owner-operator model to Paramount and WBD ’s unmatched portfolio of iconic franchises, premium original programming, and live sports rights, we can protect that legacy while building for a media landscape that’s undergoing transformational change.” The merger was set in motion about a year ago when Paramount, soon after combining with the previous incarnation of Skydance, made an unsolicited offer to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery. The overture was rebuffed multiple times, and it took more than a dozen attempts for the board of WBD to finally warm up to the deal. Along the way, a bid was accepted from Netflix to acquire just the streaming and studio side of the company. Ultimately, that proposal fell by the wayside when Paramount made its sweetened pitch to buy all of WBD. The transaction sailed through regulatory approval, only to hit a major road block in July when the attorneys general of 12 states filed a lawsuit seeking to block the deal on antitrust grounds. The Writers Guild of America filed a similar suit . Thousands of actors, writers, producers and others in the creative community signed a petition opposing the deal. It will likely remain a talking point, especially for high-profile opponents like Mark Ruffalo , who stars in HBO series Task . L-R: California AG Rob Bonta, New York AG Leticia James and David Ellison Getty Images Initially, it appeared that legal and industry objections could have a chance to derail the combination, or at least result in a shrinking of its scale. In the end, though, the AGs agreed to settle the lawsuit with only so-called “behavioral remedies” required under a 5-year consent decree . Skydance agreed to negotiate pay-TV deals for Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery as though they were still separate companies as well as supplying a minimum number of theatrical movie releases, among other concessions. Ties between the Ellisons and President Donald Trump have long been scrutinized over the course of the year-long quest for WBD by Paramount, as well as Skydance’s $8.4 billion purchase of Paramount in 2025. While Skydance has steadfastly denied it has gone out of its way to appease Trump, critics have questioned the motives behind a series of moves by David Ellison and his senior leadership team. The company, which acquired rights to the UFC mixed-martial-arts circuit last year, broadcast a live match from the White House lawn over the summer. It also acquired the Free Press, a right-leaning digital news outlet, and installed its co-founder, Bari Weiss, as editor-in-chief of CBS News despite her lack of TV experience. Paramount, during the lead-up to the deal, hosted Trump during the White House Correspondents Dinner, and Ellison also paid a visit to his compound in Mar-a-Lago. Democratic members of Congress have voiced concerns about the future of CNN, though the consent decree agreed to with the state AGs calls for an editorial oversight board to be installed. title: David Zaslav’s Farewell: Warner Bros. Discovery CEO Signs Off In Message To Staff
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News $110B Merger Of Paramount & Warner Bros Discovery Officially Closes Read the full story By Jill Goldsmith , Dade Hayes October 5, 2026 1:29pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Story Arc David Zaslav Getty/Dominic Patten/Deadline David Zaslav , Warner Bros Discovery’s CEO (for a few more hours, anyway), has started his goodbyes, thanking employees in a video posted Monday on the company’s internal portal. “It’s been a great honor to be alongside all of you,” says Zaslav, speaking from Warner Bros. Studios’ Ranch facility in Burbank. “I hope you take pride in what you’ve built, what you’ve created, and the role you’ve played in shaping an extraordinary history.” Related Stories News New Skydance Sets Top Executive Structure As Paramount-WBD Merger Set To Close Executives Ynon Kreiz Anointed Co-CEO Of New Paramount-WBD; David Ellison Says Mega-Studio Is “Transformational Moment For Our Industry” A rep from WBD declined to share a link to the video, explaining that it is intended for employees only, but Deadline has obtained a transcript. (Read it below.) The three-minute video features Zaslav sitting in a stiff-backed chair on the Warner lot, with shots of him giving remarks eventually transitioning to a series of still photographs. Multiple employees told Deadline that the photos are weighted toward award shows, red carpets and the movie and TV stars Zaslav interacted with during his tenure. Watch on Deadline The CEO, who became an unexpected (and ultimately controversial) Hollywood kingpin with the acquisition of WarnerMedia from AT&T by the much smaller Discovery in April 2022, is exiting with a large gold parachute. The Paramount -WBD deal is due to close Tuesday, less than eight months after Zaslav and the WBD board inked a deal to sell the company to David Ellison’s studio. After taking the helm, Zaslav bought an L.A. home, had Jack Warner’s old desk moved into his office on the Burbank lot and set about paring down the company’s massive debt of more than $50 billion. A substantial amount of the debt remains and will be absorbed by the new Skydance , whose debt load of $80 billion leaves little room for error as it looks to cut costs and boost streaming profits. WBD had previously planned to split in half, separating studios and streaming from cable networks, and the company later agreed to sell the former to Netflix. Ellison continued to bid for the combined company and was ultimately able to elbow his way in and seal the deal, which is valued at $110 billion. It was a rich transaction for WBD stockholders, who will get a $31-a-share payout. (WBD finished its last day as a publicly traded stock at $30.95.) Zaslav in particular stands to reap hundreds of millions from his shepherding of the deal, with the official figure to be disclosed in SEC filings over the coming days.

title: Clockwork, Warner Bros’ New Specialty Label, Is Making Jump To Skydance – The Dish
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News $110B Merger Of Paramount & Warner Bros Discovery Officially Closes Read the full story By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony ‘Verity’ Lures 2nd Best Opening For Colleen Hoover Pic With $62M+ WW; ‘Digger’ DOA At $20M WW – Top 10 Global Box Office Update Clockwork, Warner Bros’ New Specialty Label, Is Making Jump To Skydance – The Dish ‘The Batman Part II’ Production Paused As Matt Reeves Steps Away For Personal Reasons View All October 5, 2026 2:23pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Story Arc Warner Bros./Getty Images EXCLUSIVE: Warner Bros’ new Christian Parkes -led contemporary film label Clockwork , which we first told you about in December , will be making the segue to the newly merged Paramount-Warner Bros company now known as Skydance . Clockwork was on an internal list of Warner Bros labels shown in-house at Paramount. In addition, we’ve heard from reliable sources that all Warner Bros label heads (i.e., James Gunn and Peter Safran at DC, Richard Brener at New Line, etc) will stay in charge of their domains at the new conglomerate. As previously reported, all film label heads roll up and report to Paramount Pictures co-chairs Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein . Related Stories Executives James Gunn & Peter Safran To Stay At DC Studios After Paramount-Warner Bros Merger Executives New Line Boss Richard Brener Poised To Jump To Merged Paramount-Warner Bros – The Dish Clockwork’s first theatrical release is due October 16 with the unearthed 1971 Ken Russell-directed spicy Catholic taboo pic The Devils, which will be screened in a 4K restoration. The whole idea why former Warner Bros Motion Picture bosses Michael De Luca and Pamela Abdy launched the label with former Neon Chief Marketing Officer Parkes was to give the studio some A24-like mojo shots in the arm. Clockwork is an entry point for edgy filmmakers and their pics with moderate-sized budgets. The label’s original output was for two-to-three films annually. Watch on Deadline When the label was first announced in December (the name followed at CinemaCon), there was some in town who wondered whether the new indie division would make the transition in any Warner Bros. merger. Paramount currently sees Clockwork as a blooming rose. Clockwork, we understand, will co-exist with Paramount’s current global acquisition division and Republic Pictures, led by Wicker producer Lia Buman. That Melrose lot department made a big purchase out of Cannes with StudioCanal’s Midnight Library for $36 million (which includes domestic and a bulk of foreign). In addition, Republic Pictures is the label responsible for the 2024 Oscar-nominated Munich Olympics thriller September 5. Projects coming into Paramount from Clockwork include the next movie from Anora Oscar winner Sean Baker, Ti Amo! (financed by FilmNation). There’s also Clockwork’s mid-teen millions North American pick-up out of the Cannes market, Park Chan-Wook’s western The Brigands of Rattlecreek starring Matthew McConaughey , Austin Butler , Pedro Pascal and Chinese star Tang Wei ( Decision to Leave ). Also in the Clockwork portfolio is the Sean Penn-directed feature about the January 6th Capitol riots. Let’s also not forget the Mary Bronstein directed Nasty starring Jenna Ortega and Rose Byrne from producers LuckyChap; that project now in prep. Paramount didn’t return request for comment. Discovery When Skydance confirmed the company’s executive leadership team Monday, most industry reaction centered on elevated roles for content execs such as Casey Bloys, Channing Dungey and George Cheeks. But another exec in a key new post is JB Perrette , a veteran of streaming since its earliest days and a close associate of Warner Bros. Discovery CEO David Zaslav . He not only is making the leap to the new company from a top position at WBD — something of a surprise given that execs at the company being acquired generally head for the exits — but his turf also is expanding in some intriguing ways. Related Stories News Post-Merger Skydance Keeping Both HBO Max & Paramount+ Streaming Brands Executives David Zaslav’s Farewell: Warner Bros. Discovery CEO Signs Off In Message To Staff Skydance is due to close the deal Tuesday morning, and Perrette will join Co-CEOs David Ellison , Ynon Kreiz and others at a press conference later that afternoon on the Paramount lot. Watch on Deadline Upon the close of the $110 billion deal, Perrette will be Co-Chair & Chief Business Officer, Skydance DTC and Co-Chair & Chief Business Officer, Skydance TV. He will have direct global oversight of distribution, advertising sales, content sales, DTC strategy, marketing and business operations. Perrette is poised to benefit handsomely from the merger. An SEC filing in March said he would receive $142 million in various deal-related proceeds, though some portion of that could be deferred given his post in the new company. One source cited the massive payday as a potential motivating factor. “He certainly didn’t need the money,” the person said. “He obviously felt compelled by the opportunity.”
